results.content: # Pyrobuilds: Speeding Up the Exploration of Large Configuration Spaces with Incremental Build. Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN*. Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN*. Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN*. Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN*. Software developers are acutely aware that software build is an essential but resource-intensive step in any software development process, all the more when building large and/or highly configurable systems, whose vast number of configuration options leads to an explosion in the number of variants to build and evaluate. A potential approach to speed up the builds of multiple configurations is to do incremental build, i.e., to not clean the build environment and reuse previous builds artifact. This paper presents PYROBUILDS, a new approach to speed up incremental builds while keeping reproducibility, featuring a configuration variation operator parameterized by two deny lists of problematic options and a mutation size. We evaluate PYROBUILDS through an empirical study on three large configurable systems, namely Linux, BusyBox, and ToyBox, with respectively 18637, 1078, 330 options. We first show that for all configurations PYROBUILDS produces the exact same binaries as a clean build, except for Linux with some random configurations. We identify the reasons why incremental build speeds up or slows down the builds -- a knowledge that can be integrated into PYROBUILDS. We also show that a naive use of incremental build on random Linux configurations takes more time than clean builds. Thus, PYROBUILDS avoids too many differences across configurations to perform efficient incremental builds. PYROBUILDS significantly speeds up in build time from 16% to 22% in all three systems with mutated configurations. Finally, with random configurations, it also speeds up the build time from 15% to 20% for Toybox and Busybox. **Keywords:** Software Product Line, Highly-configurable Systems, Incremental Build, Build Systems. Randrianaina, Georges Aaron and Khelladi, Djamel Eddine and Zendra, Olivier and Acher, Mathieu, Pyrobuilds: Speeding Up the Exploration of Large Configuration Spaces with Incremental Build. #### Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN* ( email) ). #### Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN* ( email) ). #### Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN* ( email) ). #### Independent - *affiliation not provided to SSRN* ( email) ).

This paper presents PyroBuildS, a new approach to speed up incremental builds while keeping reproducibility, featuring a configuration variation oper-ator parameterized by two deny lists of problematic options and a mutation size (diversity). Finally, with random configura-tions, PyroBuildS also speeds up the build time from 15% to 20% for ToyBox and BusyBox. Keywords: Software Product Line, Highly-configurable Systems, Incremental Build, Build Systems 1. A key insight is that incremental builds can sometimes be more costly than traditional builds – in particular, specific problematic options hinder incremental build effectiveness and randomly selected Linux configurations often result in worse performance when built incrementally. Thus, PyroBuildS always benefits from incremental build within a local chain of variations, and optionally uses it across base configurations when it remains cost-effective. To answer our research questions, we observed three dependent variables: the build time of a configuration after both clean and incremental builds, the build reproducibility, and the diff size in terms of number of options. RQ3 – Cost reduction with random configurations To answer this research question, we report the time gains from applying PyroBuildS over fully randomly generated configurations built incrementally when compared with their own clean build time. An interesting strategy is to use random config-urations as bases (with clean build) and then incrementally build mutated configurations around, as they change an average of 3328 options (Min:Max [1795:4975]), thus diversifying the configuration space and gaining overall build time with PyroBuildS. Further results of PyroBuildS with mutation-based incremental build cannot be generalized to other small-sized configurable software system, and more experimentation remaining necessary in this area.

Title: PyroBuildS: Speeding up the exploration of large configuration spaces with incremental build - ScienceDirect
This paper presents PyroBuildS, *a new approach to speed up incremental builds* while keeping reproducibility, featuring a configuration variation operator parameterized by two deny lists of problematic options and a mutation size (diversity). We identify the reasons why incremental build speeds up or slows down the build of large configuration spaces – a knowledge that can be integrated into PyroBuildS. Thanks to its ability to operate over non-problematic options and close enough configurations, PyroBuildS significantly speeds up the exploration of large configuration spaces, with a gain in build time from 16% to 22% in all three systems with mutated configurations. As far as we know, only three studies (Randrianaina et al., 2022b, Randrianaina et al., 2022a, Lyu et al., 2024) explored the benefits of incremental build of software *configurations*. (2022b) investigated incremental build on small configurable systems with only 16 to 100 options and a few configurations. Second, *we run an in-depth empirical study of incremental build on three large complex configurable systems*, namely Linux, BusyBox, and Toybox, with respectively 18 637, 1078, 330 configuration options. When incrementally building mutated configurations, we observe a systematic gain in execution time from 16% to 22%, and a diversity in terms of options that are changed between configurations. An empirical study that investigates the general challenges of incrementally building large, complex configurable systems. PyroBuildS, an approach and tool designed to incrementally build sets of configurations – either randomly generated or systematically mutated – while controlling the generation process to favor cases where incremental builds are effective. This section describes our empirical study on the incremental build on large configurable system. **Build systems.** Many works exist on (incremental) build systems (Cao et al., 2017b, Feldman, 1979a, Tichy, 1986, Schwanke and Kaiser, 1988, Mitchell, 2012, A fast, 0000, Erdweg et al., 2015, Konat et al., 2018, Hammer et al., 2015, Maudoux and Mens, 2018) but they focus on code changes through the evolution of software (e.g. commits) rather than configurations. In this paper, we introduced PyroBuildS, an innovative approach to reduce, through incremental builds, the computational cost of building large and complex configurable systems.
